metadata.title: Micron Gains 2.4% as Memory's 86% Margin Era Refuses to Break

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU), the memory-chip manufacturer powering AI servers, climbed roughly 2.4% to $1,023.85 Wednesday. Investors are betting that scarce DRAM and high-bandwidth memory will keep prices firm well into 2027. The AI buildout still needs more memory, and Micron is selling into a market where supplynot demandis setting the pace.
The numbers explain the enthusiasm. Micron's fiscal third-quarter results delivered $41.46 billion in revenue, an 84.9% adjusted gross margin and $18.30 billion in adjusted free cash flow. Cloud-memory and core data-center sales reached $25.29 billion, or about 61% of total revenue. Management expects roughly $50 billion in fourth-quarter sales alongside an 86% gross margin.
That outlook implies another 20.6% sequential revenue surge. At $50 billion in quarterly sales, each gross-margin percentage point represents approximately $500 million of gross profit. The chart adds a valuation warning: Micron's $1,023.85 share price stands 63.58% above its $625.92 GF Value estimate. AI has turned memory into a prized capacity bottleneck, but Micron's next report must prove that exceptional pricing power can survive the industry's supply response.
